findings.title: Dependency Confusion Candidate
findings.summary: acme-internal-auth looks internal and is not registered on PyPI; resolved by version range.
findings.why_flagged: The name matches internal naming patterns (Name contains 'internal') and PyPI returns 404 for it. Resolution: range (>=1.4); no private registry is pinned for this package.
findings.attack_vector: If a resolver ever consults PyPI for this name - a missing scope-to-registry mapping, a fallback index, or a CI job without the private registry config - anyone able to publish that unclaimed name publicly could supply a package that is installed instead of the internal one. Resolvers that prefer the highest version number are the most exposed, and install-time scripts would run with the build's privileges.

remediation.title: Use a single index for internal names

remediation.title: Replace version ranges with exact pins

remediation.title: Pin exact versions and require hashes

findings.title: Insecure Registry Transport
findings.summary: legacy-tracker is resolved over plaintext HTTP (registry.npmjs.org).
findings.why_flagged: The lockfile records an http:// registry or artifact URL. Anything on the network path can read or alter the download unless an integrity hash is verified.
findings.attack_vector: Traffic over HTTP can be intercepted and modified by a network intermediary (on-path attacker), substituting the package tarball with one containing altered or hostile code. Integrity hashes turn silent substitution into a hard failure.

evidence.label: Confidence basis
evidence.value: 0.95 = base 0.85, +0.10 observed directly in the lockfile

drivers.label: Plaintext HTTP source
drivers.detail: http://registry.npmjs.org is fetched without transport security

remediation.title: Use HTTPS registries only
remediation.detail: Change http:// registry/index URLs to https:// (and enable TLS verification); block plain-HTTP egress from build agents.

findings.title: Mixed Package Index
findings.summary: requirements.txt configures an extra index; resolution can pull from either index.
findings.why_flagged: pip (and similar tools) merge all configured indexes and choose the best candidate by version, not by index priority.
findings.attack_vector: With two indexes, a package name that exists on both is resolved by highest version, so whoever can publish a higher version to the public index can displace the private one - the classic dependency-confusion condition.

evidence.label: Confidence basis
evidence.value: 0.95 = base 0.85, +0.10 observed directly in the lockfile

drivers.label: Mixed package index
drivers.detail: Extra index https://pypi.acme.corp/simple is consulted alongside the default index

drivers.label: Internal-looking packages affected
drivers.detail: 2 internal-looking name(s) can be satisfied by either index

remediation.title: Remove --extra-index-url
remediation.detail: Use one index that proxies PyPI and hosts internal packages; pip merges indexes and picks the highest version.

remediation.title: Require hashes
remediation.detail: Install with --require-hashes so only artifacts you approved can be installed from any index.

findings.title: Registered Look-alikes of express

findings.why_flagged: RIPPLE generated typo, homoglyph, separator and prefix/suffix variants of express and asked the public npm registry which exist. 2 do; the highest-scoring shows Registered on public registry; High similarity; Insertion mutation; Recent registration.
findings.attack_vector: Look-alike packages wait for a mistyped install command or a copy-pasted name.
